q: The Railway Convention Committee is:

options.A: A standing committee of Parliament, like the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: An ad hoc committee constituted from time to time by a resolution adopted by Parliament
options.C: A committee of the Railway Board
options.D: A statutory body constituted under the Railways Act, 1989

e: The Railway Convention Committee is an ad hoc committee constituted from time to time by a resolution adopted by Parliament; it is not a standing committee like the Public Accounts Committee.

q: An 'adverse balance' under a suspense or remittance head of account means a balance:

options.A: Which has been outstanding for more than one year
options.B: For which supporting vouchers are not available
options.C: Shown under the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Of a nature opposite to the normal balance of that head, requiring immediate investigation and clearance

e: An adverse balance under a suspense or remittance head is a balance of a nature opposite to the normal balance of that head; it is abnormal and requires immediate investigation and clearance.

q: In the Government system of classification of accounts, Major Head 8658 relates to:

options.A: Stores and workshop manufacture
options.B: Railway earnings
options.C: Deposits under the Public Account
options.D: Suspense Accounts

e: In the Government system of classification of accounts, Major Head 8658 relates to Suspense Accounts.

q: When the commercial accounts of Railways are combined with the Government accounts of the Union, the balances appearing under 'link heads' in the commercial accounts:

options.A: Are carried forward as assets of the Railways
options.B: Are transferred to the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Are set off and eliminated against the corresponding heads in the Government accounts
options.D: Are written off to revenue

e: When the commercial accounts of Railways are combined with the Government accounts of the Union, the balances under link heads are set off and eliminated against the corresponding heads in the Government accounts, to avoid double counting.

q: The accounts of a financial year on Indian Railways are finally closed with:

options.A: The December accounts of the year
options.B: The March (Final) accounts, incorporating supplementary adjustments after the preliminary March accounts
options.C: The June accounts of the following year
options.D: The preparation of the Appropriation Accounts

e: The accounts of a financial year on Indian Railways are finally closed with the March (Final) accounts, which incorporate supplementary adjustments made after the preliminary March accounts.

q: Expenditure is rightly treated as capital expenditure when it:

options.A: Creates an asset, or adds to the value or earning capacity of the undertaking
options.B: Exceeds a prescribed monetary limit
options.C: Is incurred through a works contract
options.D: Is incurred in the first year of a scheme

e: Expenditure is rightly treated as capital expenditure when it creates an asset, or adds to the value or earning capacity of the undertaking; expenditure that merely maintains existing assets is revenue expenditure.

q: Where a work involves both renewal of an existing asset and an improvement over the original asset, the cost is apportioned so that:

options.A: The entire cost is charged to Capital
options.B: The entire cost is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: The entire cost is charged to revenue
options.D: The cost of the asset replaced is charged to the renewal head (Depreciation Reserve Fund), and the balance representing the improvement is charged to Capital or the Development Fund

e: Where a work involves both renewal and improvement, the cost is apportioned: the cost of the asset replaced is charged to the renewal head, the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and the balance representing the improvement is charged to Capital or the Development Fund.

q: The cost of surveys and investigations carried out for a project which is ultimately abandoned is charged to:

options.A: Capital
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: Revenue
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: The cost of surveys and investigations for a project which is ultimately abandoned creates no asset, so it is charged to revenue and not to Capital.

q:
'Unsanctioned expenditure', as reported upon by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, includes expenditure incurred:
1. Without the sanction of the competent authority.
2. In excess of the amount sanctioned.
3. Under the sanction of an authority not competent to accord it.
Which of the above are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: All three are correct: unsanctioned expenditure, as reported by the CAG, includes expenditure incurred without the sanction of the competent authority, expenditure in excess of the amount sanctioned, and expenditure under the sanction of an authority not competent to accord it.

q: Re-appropriation of funds between different heads of account:

options.A: Is not permissible from a 'charged' appropriation to a 'voted' grant, or vice versa
options.B: Is freely permissible between charged appropriations and voted grants
options.C: Can be made only with the approval of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Can be made by the FA&CAO without any restriction

e: Re-appropriation of funds is not permissible from a charged appropriation to a voted grant, or vice versa, because charged and voted provisions are authorised by Parliament in different ways.

q: Guarantees given by the Government of India, including those in respect of borrowings for railway projects, are:

options.A: A part of the public debt of India
options.B: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Contingent liabilities, disclosed in the budget documents, which do not form part of the public debt
options.D: Deposits held in the Public Account of India

e: Guarantees given by the Government of India are contingent liabilities: they are disclosed in the budget documents but do not form part of the public debt, since no liability arises unless the guarantee is invoked.

q: Advances granted to Government servants, such as House Building Advance, are accounted for in the Government accounts under:

options.A: Revenue receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The 'Loans and Advances' section of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Railway suspense heads

e: Advances granted to Government servants, such as House Building Advance, are accounted for under the Loans and Advances section of the Consolidated Fund of India, and are recovered from the servants concerned.

q: The separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India took effect from the year:
e: The separation of Railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India took effect from the year 1924-25, following the Separation Convention based on the Acworth Committee's recommendations.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the annual accounts compiled in respect of Indian Railways?

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Appropriation Accounts
options.C: Finance Accounts (in so far as they relate to Railways)
options.D: Block Account, forming part of the Balance Sheet

e: The Works Register is only a register of works expenditure maintained in the divisions; it is not an annual account. The annual accounts are the Appropriation Accounts, the Finance Accounts relating to Railways, and the Block Account.

q: The statutory auditors of a Government company are appointed by:

options.A: The Board of Directors of the company
options.B: The shareholders at the annual general meeting
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs

e: The statutory auditors of a Government company are appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, who also directs the manner in which the audit is conducted.

q: The audit of the accounts of a body or authority which is substantially financed by grants or loans from the Consolidated Fund of India is undertaken by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India under the provisions of:

options.A: The Companies Act, 2013
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971
options.C: The General Financial Rules, 2017
options.D: The Railways Act, 1989

e: The audit of a body or authority substantially financed by grants or loans from the Consolidated Fund of India is undertaken by the CAG under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

q: An audit objection raised during local audit assumes the form of an 'Audit Para' when:

options.A: The reply of the executive to the objection is delayed
options.B: The amount involved in the objection is large
options.C: The Inspection Report is signed by the audit officer
options.D: The objection is included in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India laid before Parliament

e: An audit objection assumes the form of an Audit Para when the objection is included in the Report of the CAG laid before Parliament, and thereafter comes up before the Public Accounts Committee.

q: The classification of transactions in Railway accounts follows the same major and minor head structure as the Government accounts of the Union so that:

options.A: The transactions of Railways can be incorporated in the general accounts of the Union Government
options.B: Each zonal railway can evolve its own classification
options.C: Railway accounts are kept outside the Finance Accounts of the Union
options.D: Suspense heads need not be operated in railway accounts

e: The classification of transactions in Railway accounts follows the same major and minor head structure as the Government accounts of the Union, so that railway transactions can be incorporated in the general accounts of the Union Government.

q: The unspent balance of a grant remaining at the close of the financial year:

options.A: Is automatically carried forward to the next year
options.B: Lapses, and is not available for expenditure in the next year unless voted afresh by Parliament
options.C: Is credited to the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Is transferred to the Development Fund of Railways

e: The unspent balance of a grant lapses at the close of the financial year; it is not carried forward and is available in the next year only if voted afresh by Parliament.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the expenditure of the Ministry of Railways is voted by Parliament:

options.A: Through a separate Railway Budget, as before the merger
options.B: Only through the Finance Bill
options.C: As Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways forming part of the Union Budget
options.D: On the recommendation of the Railway Convention Committee

e: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the expenditure of the Ministry of Railways is voted by Parliament as Demands for Grants of that Ministry forming part of the Union Budget.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the scope of the audit of receipts conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

options.A: It is limited to verifying the arithmetical accuracy of the cash books of collecting offices
options.B: It extends to satisfying himself that all revenues and receipts due to Government are regularly recovered and credited, and that refunds of revenue are properly sanctioned
options.C: It includes fixing the rates of fares and freight to be charged by the Railways
options.D: It covers only the receipts accounted for in the Public Account of India

e: Receipt audit extends to satisfying the CAG that all revenues and receipts due to Government are regularly recovered and credited, and that refunds of revenue are properly sanctioned.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In receipt audit, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines whether adequate rules and procedures exist to secure an effective check on the assessment, collection and proper allocation of revenue, and whether they are duly observed.
2. Receipt audit requires the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to re-assess every individual assessment made by the department.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: receipt audit examines whether adequate rules and procedures exist for assessment, collection and allocation of revenue, and whether they are duly observed. Statement 2 is false: the CAG does not re-assess every individual assessment.

q: In the audit of stores and stock, the scrutiny of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is directed mainly to ensuring that:

options.A: Stores are invariably purchased at the lowest rates available
options.B: Stock verifiers are appointed in time by the executive
options.C: Physical verification of stock is carried out by the audit parties themselves
options.D: The rules regulating the custody, receipt and issue of stores are observed and the stock accounts are correctly maintained

e: In the audit of stores and stock, the CAG's scrutiny is directed mainly to ensuring that the rules regulating the custody, receipt and issue of stores are observed and that the stock accounts are correctly maintained.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Physical verification of stores and stock is the responsibility of the executive, carried out through the stock-holding officials and stock verifiers.
2. The audit of stores and stock by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India dispenses with the necessity of departmental stock verification.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: physical verification of stores and stock is the responsibility of the executive, carried out through stock-holding officials and stock verifiers. Statement 2 is false: audit by the CAG does not dispense with the necessity of departmental stock verification.

q: The audit which culminates in the certificate of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts is known as:

options.A: Performance audit
options.B: Certification (financial attest) audit
options.C: Propriety audit
options.D: Local audit

e: The audit which culminates in the certificate of the CAG on the Finance Accounts and the Appropriation Accounts is known as certification, or financial attest, audit.

q: A Utilisation Certificate furnished by a grantee institution in respect of a grant-in-aid serves as evidence for audit that:

options.A: The grant has been repaid to the Government
options.B: The grantee institution is financially sound
options.C: The grant was utilised for the purpose for which it was sanctioned
options.D: The amount of the grant was correctly estimated

e: A Utilisation Certificate furnished by a grantee institution serves as evidence for audit that the grant-in-aid was utilised for the purpose for which it was sanctioned.

q: For externally aided projects executed by Railways, the audit certificate on the project accounts and expenditure, required by the funding agency, is issued by:

options.A: The FA&CAO of the Railway
options.B: The funding agency itself
options.C: The Railway Board
options.D: The audit organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: For externally aided projects executed by Railways, the audit certificate on the project accounts and expenditure, required by the funding agency, is issued by the audit organisation of the CAG of India.

q: The resident audit organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on a zonal Railway is headed by the:

options.A: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.B: Principal Director of Audit
options.C: Financial Commissioner (Railways)
options.D: Chief Auditor of the Railway

e: The resident audit organisation of the CAG on a zonal Railway is headed by the Principal Director of Audit.

q: An Inspection Report issued after local audit is addressed to:

options.A: The head of the office or unit audited, who is responsible for furnishing replies and taking remedial action
options.B: The Public Accounts Committee
options.C: The Railway Board in all cases
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: An Inspection Report issued after local audit is addressed to the head of the office or unit audited, who is responsible for furnishing replies and taking remedial action on the objections.

q: An audit objection raised in an Inspection Report is treated as settled only when:

options.A: The audited office sends any reply to the objection
options.B: One year has passed since the objection was raised
options.C: The audit office, on examining the reply and the action taken by the executive, accepts it and drops the objection
options.D: The FA&CAO certifies that action has been taken on the objection

e: An audit objection is treated as settled only when the audit office, on examining the reply and the action taken by the executive, accepts it and drops the objection; a mere reply does not settle it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An audit objection involving a loss to the Railways is not finally settled merely by the passage of time; the loss has to be recovered or its write-off sanctioned by the competent authority.
2. The settlement of an audit objection rests with the audit office, which drops the objection when it is satisfied with the action taken by the executive.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a loss objection is not settled by mere passage of time - the loss must be recovered or written off under competent sanction; and settlement rests with the audit office, which drops the objection when satisfied.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Test audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relieves the Railway Accounts Department of its responsibility for cent-per-cent internal check of transactions.
2. Under test audit, the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India checks a selected portion of the transactions instead of checking every transaction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: test audit by the CAG does not relieve the Railway Accounts Department of its responsibility for cent-per-cent internal check. Statement 2 is true: under test audit, only a selected portion of the transactions is checked by the CAG's organisation.

q: The extent of test check exercised by audit in a unit is determined largely by:

options.A: The assessed strength of the system of internal check and internal control operating in the unit
options.B: The age of the building in which the office is housed
options.C: The number of officers posted in the unit
options.D: The alphabetical order in which the units are taken up for audit

e: The extent of test check exercised by audit in a unit is determined largely by the assessed strength of the system of internal check and internal control operating in that unit; the stronger the control, the smaller the test check required.

q: Appropriation audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India includes verifying that:

options.A: The total expenditure of the Government is kept within the total Budget of the year
options.B: Every estimate sanctioned during the year was framed correctly
options.C: The staff sanctioned for each office is adequate for its work
options.D: Expenditure has been booked under the correct head of account, so that it is counted against the proper grant or appropriation

e: Appropriation audit includes verifying that expenditure has been booked under the correct head of account, so that it is counted against the proper grant or appropriation authorised by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An excess of expenditure under one grant is not condoned merely because there are savings under another grant; the excess requires regularisation through an Excess Grant.
2. Appropriation audit is concerned not only with the total expenditure against a grant, but also with the expenditure booked under its constituent heads.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: an excess under one grant is not condoned merely because there are savings under another grant and requires regularisation through an Excess Grant; and appropriation audit covers expenditure under the constituent heads of a grant, not only its total.

q: Expenditure on a 'new service' or 'new instrument of service' not contemplated in the Budget Estimates requires:

options.A: Only the sanction of the General Manager of the Railway
options.B: The prior approval of Parliament before the expenditure is incurred
options.C: Only the concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: No approval, if the amount involved is small

e: Expenditure on a new service or new instrument of service not contemplated in the Budget Estimates requires the prior approval of Parliament before the expenditure is incurred.

q: Along with the Appropriation Accounts, which of the following documents is laid before Parliament in respect of the accounts of the Union?

options.A: The Finance Accounts
options.B: The Works Register
options.C: The Station Balance Sheet
options.D: The Pink Book

e: Along with the Appropriation Accounts, the Finance Accounts of the Union are also laid before Parliament in respect of the accounts of the Union.

q: Which of the following forms part of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government?

options.A: The contractor's ledger of each division
options.B: The station balance sheets of the Railways
options.C: A statement showing the position of the public debt of the Government of India
options.D: The labour pay sheets of workshops

e: A statement showing the position of the public debt of the Government of India forms part of the Finance Accounts of the Union Government.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Interest and other debt charges for which the Government of India is liable are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Charged expenditure is included in the Appropriation Act, although it is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: interest and other debt charges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; and charged expenditure, though not submitted to the vote of Parliament, is included in the Appropriation Act.

q: Amounts advanced from the Contingency Fund of India to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure are recouped to the Fund:

options.A: Automatically at the close of the financial year
options.B: After Parliament has authorised the expenditure, by appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Only after the Comptroller and Auditor General of India certifies the accounts
options.D: Out of the Public Account of India

e: Amounts advanced from the Contingency Fund of India are recouped to the Fund after Parliament has authorised the expenditure, by appropriation from the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: In respect of the moneys kept in the Public Account of India, the Government acts in the capacity of:

options.A: The owner of the moneys
options.B: A guarantor of the depositors
options.C: An agent of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: A banker or trustee, being liable to repay the moneys to the depositors

e: In respect of moneys kept in the Public Account of India, such as Provident Fund deposits, the Government acts as a banker or trustee: it is not the owner of the moneys and is liable to repay them to the depositors.

q: The separation convention of 1924, governing the financial relations between Railways and General Finances, was first revised after Independence by the Railway Convention Committee of:
e: The Separation Convention of 1924 was first revised after Independence by the Railway Convention Committee of 1949, which settled the financial relations between Railways and General Finances for the post-Independence period.

q: Under the financial convention between Railways and General Finances, as it stood before the merger of the Railway Budget, the surplus earned by Railways after payment of dividend was:

options.A: Distributed among the States
options.B: Retained by Railways, being credited mainly to the Development Fund for improvement works
options.C: Lapsed to the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: Paid to the railway staff as bonus

e: Under the financial convention, the surplus earned by Railways after payment of dividend was retained by Railways, being credited mainly to the Development Fund for improvement works.

q: Before its abolition, the dividend payable by Railways to General Finances was computed on the capital-at-charge:

options.A: Including the capital invested in strategic lines
options.B: Excluding the capital invested in strategic lines
options.C: Consisting only of market borrowings
options.D: Consisting only of revenue reserves

e: Before its abolition, the dividend payable by Railways to General Finances was computed on the capital-at-charge excluding the capital invested in strategic lines, which are maintained for defence rather than commercial return.

q: Apart from dividend, Railways also made a 'payment in lieu of tax' to General Finances, which was related to:

options.A: Passenger fares
options.B: Freight earnings
options.C: Catering receipts
options.D: Parcel earnings

e: Apart from dividend, Railways also made a payment in lieu of tax to General Finances, which was related to passenger fares, corresponding to the tax that would otherwise have been leviable on them.

q: Which of the following does NOT form part of the capital-at-charge of Railways?

options.A: Capital expenditure on construction of new lines
options.B: Capital works financed from the Capital Fund
options.C: Cost of renewals and replacements financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Capital expenditure on rolling stock

e: The cost of renewals and replacements financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund does not form part of capital-at-charge, because such renewals merely restore assets whose original cost already stands included in the capital-at-charge.

q: The Block Account of a Railway shows, for each class of asset:

options.A: Only the additions made during the year
options.B: The stores held in stock in depots
options.C: The grants blocked by Parliament during the year
options.D: The opening balance, additions during the year and the closing balance of the capital invested

e: The Block Account of a Railway shows, for each class of asset, the opening balance, the additions during the year and the closing balance of the capital invested in that class.

q: A work is chargeable to the Development Fund of Railways when it is:

options.A: A work creating a new asset of lasting value
options.B: A renewal of an existing asset
options.C: An improvement or amenity work which does not qualify for charge to Capital or to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: A track renewal work

e: A work is chargeable to the Development Fund when it is an improvement or amenity work which does not qualify for charge to Capital, as it creates no new asset, or to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, as it is not a renewal.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Capital Fund from the Development Fund on Railways?

options.A: Works financed from the Capital Fund are of a capital nature, financed from internal resources, while the Development Fund finances improvement and amenity works
options.B: The Capital Fund finances staff quarters only, while the Development Fund finances track works
options.C: There is no difference between the two funds
options.D: The Development Fund finances capital works, while the Capital Fund finances amenity works

e: Works financed from the Capital Fund are of a capital nature, financed from internal resources, while the Development Fund finances improvement and amenity works; this is the essential distinction between the two funds.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the railway accounts, assets continue to be shown in the Block Account at their original capital cost.
2. Depreciation of railway assets is provided by annual appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, assessed with reference to the life of the assets.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: assets continue to be shown in the Block Account at their original capital cost, and depreciation is provided by annual appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, assessed with reference to asset life.

q: Under the system of depreciation accounting followed on Railways, an asset whose normal life has expired but which continues in service:

options.A: Is written off the Block Account automatically
options.B: Continues to be borne on the Block Account at its original cost until it is actually replaced or renewed
options.C: Is revalued every year at the market price
options.D: Is transferred to the Public Account of India

e: Under the codal-life system, expiry of an asset's prescribed life does not by itself remove it from the books: it continues to be borne on the Block Account at original cost and is written off only when actually replaced or renewed.

q: Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund from revenue are assessed with reference to:

options.A: The market value of the assets
options.B: The rate of dividend payable to General Finances
options.C: The savings available in the revenue budget
options.D: The prescribed life of each class of asset

e: The annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed class-wise with reference to the prescribed life of each asset, so that the fund accumulates enough to finance its replacement by the time its life expires.

q: The capital expenditure of Railways is financed through a combination of:

options.A: Gross Budgetary Support, internal resources and Extra Budgetary Resources
options.B: Only loans from the World Bank
options.C: Only passenger fare receipts
options.D: Only grants from the State Governments

e: Railway capital expenditure is financed from three sources combined: Gross Budgetary Support from the General Budget, the Railways' own internal resources, and Extra Budgetary Resources such as market borrowings raised through IRFC.

q: The liability for servicing (interest and repayment) the Extra Budgetary Resources raised for railway projects rests on:

options.A: The general budget alone, with no charge on the Railways
options.B: The Railways, through provision made in the Railway Budget
options.C: The State Governments
options.D: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: Borrowings raised as Extra Budgetary Resources are serviced by the Railways themselves: interest and repayment are provided for in the Railway Budget through lease and debt-service charges, and are not borne by General Finances.

q: The Indian Railway Finance Corporation finances the acquisition of rolling stock for Railways mainly by:

options.A: Budgetary grants from the Ministry of Finance
options.B: Levying a surcharge on passenger fares
options.C: Raising funds from the capital market through bonds and other borrowings
options.D: Selling surplus railway land

e: IRFC raises resources from the capital market by issuing bonds and other borrowings, and deploys them to finance the acquisition of rolling stock for the Railways under lease arrangements.

q: Under the standard lease arrangement between IRFC and the Ministry of Railways, during the period of the lease:

options.A: The rolling stock is owned by the Railways from the date of its acquisition
options.B: The rolling stock is owned jointly by IRFC and the Railways
options.C: The rolling stock stands transferred to the State Governments
options.D: The rolling stock remains the property of IRFC, and the Railways pay lease charges to IRFC

e: Under the standard lease, ownership of the financed rolling stock vests in IRFC during the lease period; the Railways use the stock and pay lease charges covering principal and interest to IRFC.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The lease charges payable to IRFC, comprising principal and interest, are met from the Railway Budget.
2. On the expiry of the lease period, the financed rolling stock is transferred to the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the lease charges payable to IRFC, comprising principal and interest, are met from the Railway Budget, and on expiry of the lease the financed rolling stock is transferred to the Railways.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the recognised heads of scrutiny in the audit of expenditure conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?

options.A: Audit against provision of funds
options.B: Audit against sanctions
options.C: Audit against rules and orders
options.D: Audit against the commercial policy of the undertaking

e: Audit of expenditure is conducted against provision of funds, sanctions, rules and orders, and propriety. Judging the commercial policy of an undertaking is the executive's domain and is not a recognised head of CAG audit scrutiny.

q: The Railway Safety Fund is credited mainly with:

options.A: The dividend received from railway public sector undertakings
options.B: The sale proceeds of scrap
options.C: Market borrowings raised through IRFC
options.D: The proceeds of the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares

e: The Railway Safety Fund, used for safety works at level crossings, is credited mainly with the proceeds of the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares.

q: An audit objection of sufficient importance, which remains unsettled after the executive's reply, may be:

options.A: Written off automatically after one year
options.B: Settled by the FA&CAO on behalf of audit
options.C: Sent directly to the Public Accounts Committee by the audited office
options.D: Developed by the audit office into a Draft Para for possible inclusion in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: An important audit objection that remains unsettled after the executive's reply is developed by the audit office into a Draft Para, which may find place in the Report of the CAG laid before the legislature.

q: A local audit (inspection) party of the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is ordinarily headed by:

options.A: The FA&CAO of the Railway
options.B: A Section Officer of the Railway Accounts Department
options.C: The head of the office being audited
options.D: An Audit Officer of the audit office

e: A local audit (inspection) party of the CAG's organisation, which inspects the accounts and records of a unit on the spot, is ordinarily headed by an Audit Officer of the audit office.

q: An order of re-appropriation of funds within a grant, to be valid, must be issued:

options.A: Within three years of the expenditure
options.B: After the accounts of the year are closed
options.C: Only by Parliament
options.D: Before the expiry of the financial year to which it relates

e: A re-appropriation order is valid only if issued before the expiry of the financial year to which the grant relates; after the year closes, the grant lapses and no re-appropriation can be made.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Finance Accounts from the Appropriation Accounts of the Union?

options.A: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the Government as a whole, while the Appropriation Accounts compare the expenditure with the grants and appropriations for each service
options.B: The Finance Accounts relate only to Railways, while the Appropriation Accounts relate only to Defence
options.C: The Finance Accounts are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, while the Appropriation Accounts are prepared by Parliament
options.D: There is no difference between the two documents

e: The Finance Accounts present the receipts and disbursements of the Government as a whole, whereas the Appropriation Accounts compare, service-wise, the actual expenditure with the grants and appropriations sanctioned for each service.

q: In auditing grants-in-aid given to a body or institution, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India examines, among other things, whether:

options.A: The body has earned a profit during the year
options.B: The grant was utilised for the purpose, and subject to the conditions, on which it was sanctioned
options.C: The staff of the body are working efficiently
options.D: The grant should be enhanced in the next year

e: In auditing grants-in-aid, the CAG examines whether the grant was utilised for the purpose for which, and subject to the conditions under which, it was sanctioned; diversion or misuse is taken up in audit.

q: In the 'audit against sanctions', the audit office examines whether:

options.A: The sanction for the expenditure was issued by an authority competent to issue it and conforms to the applicable rules
options.B: The work was completed ahead of schedule
options.C: The lowest tender was accepted in every case
options.D: The number of staff in the office is adequate for its work

e: In audit against sanctions, the audit office verifies that the sanction authorising the expenditure was issued by an authority competent to issue it and that the sanction conforms to the applicable rules and orders.

q: Article 266(3) of the Constitution lays down that no moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India shall be appropriated except:

options.A: Under an executive order of the Finance Minister
options.B: In accordance with law, that is, under the authority of an Appropriation Act passed by Parliament
options.C: Under a resolution of the Lok Sabha alone
options.D: With the prior concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Article 266(3) prohibits appropriation of moneys out of the Consolidated Fund of India except in accordance with law, that is, under an Appropriation Act passed by Parliament after the Demands for Grants are voted.

q: The Contingency Fund of India, referred to in the Constitution, is established:

options.A: By Parliament, by law, under Article 267
options.B: By the President, by an ordinance
options.C: By a notification of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: By a resolution of the Railway Board

e: Article 267 empowers Parliament to establish, by law, a Contingency Fund of India, placed at the disposal of the President to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament.

q: Under Article 148 of the Constitution, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President:

options.A: On the recommendation of the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: By a resolution of both Houses of Parliament
options.C: By warrant under his hand and seal
options.D: On the advice of the Finance Commission

e: Under Article 148, the CAG is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, a form that underlines the constitutional status and independence of the office.

q: Under Article 113 of the Constitution, no demand for a grant shall be made except:

options.A: With the approval of the Estimates Committee
options.B: With the concurrence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: After the general discussion on the Budget is over
options.D: On the recommendation of the President

e: Article 113 provides that no demand for a grant shall be made except on the recommendation of the President, ensuring that proposals for expenditure originate with the executive.

q: In respect of the Appropriation Bill, Article 114 of the Constitution provides that:

options.A: No amendment shall be proposed in either House which will have the effect of varying the amount or altering the destination of any grant, or varying the amount of any charged expenditure
options.B: Amendments can be moved freely in the Rajya Sabha only
options.C: The Bill cannot be introduced in an election year
options.D: The Bill is certified as a Money Bill by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Article 114 bars any amendment to the Appropriation Bill that would vary the amount or alter the destination of a grant already voted, or vary the amount of any charged expenditure.

q: Supplementary, additional or excess grants are provided for in the Constitution under:

options.A: Article 112
options.B: Article 115
options.C: Article 118
options.D: Article 266

e: Article 115 provides for supplementary, additional or excess grants where the amount authorised for a service proves insufficient, a new service arises, or expenditure exceeds the grant during the year.

q: The power of the Lok Sabha to make a vote on account, a vote of credit and an exceptional grant is conferred by:

options.A: Article 110
options.B: Article 113
options.C: Article 116
options.D: Article 280

e: Article 116 confers on the Lok Sabha the power to make a vote on account (grant in advance), a vote of credit (for an unexpected demand) and an exceptional grant (for a special purpose).

q: The Constitution protects the independence of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India by providing that his conditions of service:

options.A: Shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment
options.B: Are fixed by the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: Are revised by the Finance Commission every five years
options.D: Are the same as those of a Cabinet Secretary

e: To safeguard the CAG's independence, the Constitution provides that his salary and conditions of service shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

q: Under the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the duty of the CAG in relation to the audit of all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India is dealt with in:

options.A: Section 10
options.B: Section 14
options.C: Section 23
options.D: Section 13

e: Section 13 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 lays down the CAG's duty in relation to the audit of all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India.

q: The audit of the accounts of Government companies by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is provided for in the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 under:

options.A: Section 16
options.B: Section 19
options.C: Section 21
options.D: Section 12

e: Section 19 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 provides for the audit of the accounts of Government companies and corporations by the CAG.

q: Section 20 of the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971 relates to:

options.A: Audit of the accounts of certain authorities or bodies, not otherwise subject to audit by the CAG, entrusted to the CAG
options.B: Audit of receipts payable into the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Audit of stores and stock
options.D: The salary and allowances of the CAG

e: Section 20 of the Act relates to audit of authorities or bodies not otherwise subject to CAG audit, where such audit is entrusted to the CAG by the President, Governor or under law.

q: The salary of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is equal to the salary of:

options.A: The Chief Justice of India
options.B: A Cabinet Minister
options.C: A Judge of the Supreme Court
options.D: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India

e: The salary of the CAG is equal to the salary of a Judge of the Supreme Court, reflecting the high constitutional status attached to the office.

q: Before entering upon his office, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India makes and subscribes an oath or affirmation before:

options.A: The Chief Justice of India
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: The President of India, or some person appointed in that behalf by him

e: Under Article 148(2), before entering office the CAG makes and subscribes an oath or affirmation before the President, or a person appointed by the President for that purpose, as per the Third Schedule.

q: For the purposes of audit, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is empowered to:

options.A: Disallow any item of expenditure at his own discretion
options.B: Inspect any office of accounts and call for any accounts, books, papers and other documents required for audit
options.C: Impose penalties on the officers of the audited department
options.D: Stop payment of any bill presented to the Accounts office

e: For the purposes of audit, the CAG is empowered to inspect any office of accounts and to call for any accounts, books, papers and other documents he requires; he cannot himself disallow items or stop payments.

q: By a convention followed since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed from amongst the members belonging to:

options.A: The Opposition in the Lok Sabha
options.B: The ruling party in the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Rajya Sabha
options.D: The Estimates Committee

e: By a convention followed since 1967, the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed from amongst the members belonging to the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, strengthening parliamentary control over the executive.

q: The members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by each House of Parliament from amongst its members according to the principle of:

options.A: Simple majority in a joint sitting
options.B: Nomination by the President
options.C: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
options.D: Nomination by the Speaker and the Chairman jointly

e: Members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by each House from amongst its members according to the principle of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

q: The Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by:

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The members of the Committee themselves
options.C: The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs
options.D: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, from amongst the members of the Committee

e: The Chairperson of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee.

q: One of the functions of the Estimates Committee is to suggest:

options.A: The rate of dividend payable by Railways to General Finances
options.B: The form in which the estimates shall be presented to Parliament
options.C: The composition of the Railway Board
options.D: The fare and freight structure of Railways

e: Besides reporting on economies and efficiency, the Estimates Committee suggests the form in which the estimates shall be presented to Parliament.

q: The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of:

options.A: 22 members — 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha
options.B: 30 members, all from the Lok Sabha
options.C: 15 members, all from the Rajya Sabha
options.D: 45 members drawn from both Houses

e: The Committee on Public Undertakings consists of 22 members - 15 from the Lok Sabha and 7 from the Rajya Sabha.

q: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways examines, and reports to the Houses on:

options.A: The audit paragraphs in the Report of the CAG relating to Railways
options.B: The service records of railway officers
options.C: The Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways
options.D: The rate of return on capital-at-charge of Railways

e: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways examines the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways and reports on them to the Houses; examination of audit paragraphs is the Public Accounts Committee's field.

q: Which of the following correctly states the position of the Public Accounts Committee in relation to policy?

options.A: It examines the estimates and suggests the policy to be followed by the Government
options.B: It frames the policy underlying each Demand for Grant
options.C: It can disallow any item of expenditure on policy grounds
options.D: It examines the accounts after the expenditure is incurred and does not go into questions of policy

e: The Public Accounts Committee examines the accounts after the expenditure has been incurred, on the basis of the CAG's reports; it is a post-expenditure watchdog and does not go into questions of policy.

q: Before an audit objection is developed into a Draft Para for inclusion in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:

options.A: The para is first voted upon by the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: The facts stated in the para are got confirmed from the Ministry or department concerned, and its comments are invited
options.C: The approval of the Finance Minister is obtained
options.D: The objection is published in the Gazette of India

e: Before an audit objection is developed into a Draft Para, the facts stated in it are got confirmed from the Ministry or department concerned and its comments are invited, so that the para rests on verified facts.

q: The Action Taken Notes furnished by the Government on the paragraphs in the Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are, before being sent to the Public Accounts Committee:

options.A: Approved by the Railway Convention Committee
options.B: Certified by the FA&CAO of the Railway
options.C: Vetted by Audit
options.D: Placed before the Cabinet

e: The Action Taken Notes furnished by the Government on the CAG's report paragraphs are vetted by Audit before being sent to the Public Accounts Committee, so the Committee can judge whether the action reported is adequate.

q: Minor irregularities noticed during the test audit of accounts, which do not call for a detailed Inspection Report, are brought to the notice of the executive through:

options.A: A Test Audit Note
options.B: An Audit Para
options.C: A Draft Para
options.D: The Finance Accounts

e: Minor irregularities noticed during test audit, which are not serious enough to call for a detailed Inspection Report, are brought to the notice of the executive through a Test Audit Note.

q: 'Central audit', as distinguished from local audit, means audit:

options.A: Conducted only of the Railway Board's accounts
options.B: Conducted by the Central Government's own staff
options.C: Limited to the accounts of one selected month
options.D: Conducted at the headquarters office of the audit organisation, to which the vouchers and accounts of the units concerned are sent

e: In central audit, the vouchers and accounts of the units concerned are sent to the headquarters office of the audit organisation, where the audit is conducted, unlike local audit done at the unit itself.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India audits all transactions of the Union relating to the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The audit of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India also extends to the transactions relating to the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the CAG audits all transactions of the Union relating to the Consolidated Fund of India, and his audit also extends to transactions relating to the Contingency Fund and the Public Account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On Indian Railways, the compilation of accounts is done by the Railway Accounts Department itself, while audit is conducted by the organisation of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, so that accounting and audit stand separated.
2. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is responsible for the compilation of the accounts of Indian Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: on Railways, compilation of accounts is done by the Railway Accounts Department while audit is done by the CAG's organisation. Statement 2 is wrong - the CAG audits railway accounts but does not compile them.

q: On a zonal Railway, the FA&CAO functions as:

options.A: The head of the resident audit organisation
options.B: The principal financial adviser to the General Manager
options.C: The representative of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Chairman of the Railway Convention Committee

e: On a zonal Railway, the FA and CAO functions as the principal financial adviser to the General Manager and heads the railway's finance and accounts organisation.

q: Under the system of 'associated finance' followed on Railways:

options.A: All works are financed only from market borrowings
options.B: The concurrence of the CAG is required for every item of expenditure
options.C: The Railway Budget is associated with the General Budget for all purposes
options.D: Proposals involving financial implications require the concurrence of the associated finance (the FA&CAO's organisation) before sanction by the competent executive authority

e: Under associated finance, proposals involving financial implications require the concurrence of the associated finance, that is, the FA and CAO's organisation, before sanction by the competent executive authority.

q: The internal audit organisation on a zonal Railway functions under:

options.A: The FA&CAO of the Railway
options.B: The Principal Director of Audit
options.C: The Financial Commissioner (Railways)
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

e: The internal audit organisation on a zonal Railway functions under the FA and CAO of the Railway; external audit is separately conducted by the CAG's organisation through the Principal Director of Audit.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB) formulates the Indian Government Accounting Standards (IGAS) for the Government accounts.
2. GASAB functions under the aegis of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Government Accounting Standards Advisory Board (GASAB) formulates the Indian Government Accounting Standards (IGAS), and it functions under the aegis of the CAG of India.

q: In the Balance Sheet of Indian Railways, the capital-at-charge is shown:

options.A: On the assets side, along with the Block Account
options.B: On the liabilities side
options.C: Only in the Finance Accounts of the Union
options.D: Under the Public Account of India

e: Capital-at-charge represents the Government's investment in the Railways, hence it is shown on the liabilities side of the Railway Balance Sheet, the corresponding assets being carried in the Block Account.

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund, created for clearing the backlog of safety-related renewal works, was set up following the recommendations of:

options.A: The Acworth Committee
options.B: The Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee)
options.C: The Railway Convention Committee of 1954
options.D: The Debroy Committee

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund, created for clearing the backlog of safety-related renewal works, was set up following the recommendations of the Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee).

q: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget was recommended, among others, by:

options.A: The Acworth Committee
options.B: The Kunzru Committee
options.C: The Khanna Committee
options.D: The Bibek Debroy Committee

e: The merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget was recommended by the Bibek Debroy Committee, which proposed doing away with the separate Railway Budget as part of restructuring the Railways.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget, the surplus of Railways, after meeting its working expenses, is:

options.A: Retained by Railways and appropriated to its funds, such as the DRF, Development Fund, Capital Fund and RRSK
options.B: Paid to General Finances as dividend, as before the merger
options.C: Credited to the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Distributed among the State Governments

e: After the merger, Railways no longer pay dividend to General Finances; the surplus after meeting working expenses is retained by Railways and appropriated to its funds such as the DRF, Development Fund, Capital Fund and RRSK.
